translations.text: The Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom
When the deacon enters the diaconicon, he says the prayer: O Lord my God,

send down upon me power from on high and strengthen me for this ministry of yours, so that I may stand without condemnation before your holy, dread and awesome altar and offer to you the bloodless sacrifice. For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father and of the Son

When he cuts out [the Lamb], he says: The Lamb of God, the Son of the Father, who takes away the sins of the world, is sacrificed for the life of the world. He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb is silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away; and who will declare his generation? For his life is taken away from the earth.
When he cuts out the portion of the All-Holy [Mother of God], let him say: Accept, O Lord our God, this offering through the intercession of our all-holy Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary.
Over the holy [?] let him say:
Remember, O Lord our God, your saint [Name], and accept this service of ours through his intercession.
For the departed, let him say: For the repose and blessedness and forgiveness of sins.
For all in general, let him say: Remember, O Lord, all Orthodox Christians, your servants, and give them rest in the light of your face.
They are to arrange them on the paten: the Lord's portion in the middle, the portion of the All-Holy on the right, the portion of the saint on the left, and the others as [?]
Let him pour [the wine] over it and say: One of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out. He who saw it has borne witness, and his witness is true.
The priest's prayer: We offer incense to you,
O Christ our God,
as a sweet fragrance. In return send down upon us the grace of your Holy Spirit, always, now.
Deacon: For the precious sacrifices set forth, let us pray to the Lord.

Prayer of the priest at the prothesis: O Lord our God, who sent the bread of heaven, the food of the whole world, our Lord and God Jesus Christ, as Saviour, Redeemer and Benefactor, to bless and sanctify us: bless this our offering, and at your supercelestial and spiritual altar, as a good God who loves mankind, remember those who have offered it and those for whom they offered it. Keep us without condemnation in the sacred celebration of your divine mysteries. For holy and glorified is your all-honoured and majestic name, of the Father and of the Son

The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself with majesty. The Lord has clothed himself with strength and girded himself. He has established the world so that it will not be moved. His majesty has covered the heavens, and the whole earth is filled with his praise. Amen.
Bless, master.
May the Holy Spirit celebrate together with us.
Bless, master.
Blessed is the kingdom of the Father and of the Son
For the peace from above and for the salvation of our souls, [let us pray to] the Lord
For the peace of the whole world, for the good stability of the holy churches of God, and for the union of all, [let us pray] to the Lord.
For this holy house and for those who enter it with faith, reverence and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord.
For our archbishop, the honoured priests, the deacons in Christ, and all the clergy and the people, [let us pray] to the Lord.
For our pious and God-protected king, and for all his palace and his soldiers, let us pray to the Lord.
That [the Lord] may fight alongside him against all enemies and adversaries, [let us pray] to the Lord.
For our city, for every city and village, and for those who dwell in them in faith, [let us pray] to the Lord.
For good temperate weather, for an abundant yield of fruits, and for peace in the land and in our times, [let us pray] to the Lord.
For those who sail, those who travel, the sick, those who labor, and captives, and for their deliverance and salvation, [let us pray] to the Lord.
That we may be delivered from all affliction, wrath and distress, [let us pray] to the Lord.
And for all who ask help and mercy from God, [let us pray] to the Lord.
Prayer of the priest:
O Lord our God,
whose might is immeasurable and whose glory is incomprehensible, whose mercy is countless and whose love for humankind is beyond words:
look down, O Master, in your mercy on us and on this holy house, and pour out your mercies and compassions richly on us and on those who pray with us.
Help us.
[Remembering] our all-holy, incorruptible, most blessed Lady Mary, with the saints of heaven [?], [let us commend] ourselves and one another and all our life [to Christ our God].
For to you belong all glory, honor...
Again and again, [in] peace [let us pray to the Lord].
Prayer of the priest:

O Lord our God, save your people and bless your inheritance. Preserve the fullness of your Church, and sanctify those who love the beauty of your house. You [?] them in return; do not forsake us who hope in you.
Help us.
Of the all-holy,
Of our immaculate, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary,
of the holy Forerunner and Baptist John,
remembering, together with all the saints, ourselves [?]
Again and again...
Prayer of the priest:

You who have granted us these common prayers offered with one voice, and who have promised to fulfil the requests of two or three who agree together in your name: fulfil them now for what is best [?], giving us in this present age the knowledge of your truth, and granting us eternal life in the age to come.
Help us.
Of the all-holy, immaculate [?], of the holy and all-praised apostles,
remembering them together with all the saints, [let us commit] ourselves [?]
For you are a good God, who loves humankind.
Let us pray to the Lord.
The priest's prayer: O Master,
O Lord our God,
who established in the heavens the orders and hosts of angels and archangels to serve your glory,
let holy angels enter with us as we enter, to serve with us and to join us in glorifying your goodness.
For all [glory] is fitting to you.
I worship the Father,
the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Trinity of one essence,
undivided, who reigns forever.
Prayer said by the priest:
Holy God, who rest among the saints,
who are hymned by the seraphim with the thrice-holy cry and glorified by the cherubim, [?] who brought all things out of non-existence into being,

You created man in your image and likeness and adorned him with all your grace. You give wisdom and understanding to those who ask, and you do not despise sinners but appoint repentance for their salvation.
You have made us, your lowly and unworthy servants, worthy even at this hour to stand before the glory of your holy altar and to offer you the worship and praise that are your due.
O Master, accept the thrice-holy hymn even from the mouths of us sinners, and look upon us in your sweetness. Forgive us all our transgressions, voluntary and involuntary,
and sanctify our souls and bodies, and grant us to serve you worthily all the days of our life, through the intercessions of the all-holy Mother of God and of all your saints who have pleased you.
For you are holy, our God, and we send up glory to you
Bless, Master, this throne. Blessed are you who sit upon the throne of the glory of your kingdom, always, now and
Let us attend.
Peace be to all.
The deacon: Bless us, Master.
The priest: May the Lord [?] the words to the evangelist with great power, the King of the powers of love [?], by his grace, always,
now
The deacon: O King of heaven,

O Comforter, Spirit of truth, guide of wisdom, giver of knowledge, teacher of the foolish and one who takes the poor by the hand: strengthen my soul and make it wise, O Master. Give me speech, O Word of the Father. Behold, I will not keep my lips silent from crying out to you. O Merciful One, be merciful to me, who have fallen down before you.

The priest's prayer: Shine forth in our hearts, O lover of mankind; open the eyes of my knowledge of God so that I may understand the preaching of your Gospel. Put in us the fear of your blessed commandments, so that we may trample down every fleshly desire, take up a spiritual way of life, and think and do everything that pleases you.
The deacon: Let us all say, with all our soul and with all our mind, let us all say:
O Lord Almighty, God of our fathers, we beseech you, hear us.
You who are rich in mercy and generous in compassion, we beseech you
You who do not desire the death of the sinner, but rather his turning back and repentance, we beseech you.
For this holy house
For our salvation
And [?]
Have mercy on us, O God, according to your great mercy.
We beseech you

The priest's prayer: O Lord our God, accept this earnest supplication from your servants. Have mercy on us according to the multitude of your mercies, and send down your compassion upon us and upon all your people, who wait for the rich mercy that comes from you.

The deacon: Again, for the strength, victory, stability, peace, righteousness and life of our pious and God-protected king, and that the Lord our God may help him all the more, prosper him in all his service of God, and make all his enemies and adversaries submit to him, let us all say.
Again we beseech you for the righteousness and life and the forgiveness of sins of the servant of God N., and for all our brothers, let us all say.
The priest shall make the sign of the cross over both and say the exclamation: For you are a merciful God who loves humankind, and we send up glory to you. The people: Amen.
The deacon: Pray, catechumens. You faithful, let us pray for the catechumens, that the Lord may have mercy on them,
that he may teach them the word of truth, reveal to them the gospel of righteousness, and unite them to his holy apostolic Church.
Save them, have mercy on them, and protect them, O God, by your grace.
Catechumens, bow your heads to the Lord.

The priest says the prayer before the offering: O Lord our God, who dwell on high and look upon the lowly, who sent your only-begotten, our God and Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of the human race: look upon your servants the catechumens, who have bowed their necks to you. Make them worthy, at the right time, of the font of the second birth, the forgiveness of sins, and the garment of incorruption. Unite them to your holy catholic and apostolic Church, and number them with your chosen flock.
Exclamation: So that these too, with us, may glorify your all-honorable and majestic name, of the Father
The deacon: All who are catechumens, depart. Catechumens, depart. All who are catechumens, depart. Let none of the catechumens
but as many as are faithful, again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord.
The priest, a prayer:
We thank you,

O Lord of hosts, who have made us worthy to stand even now at your holy altar and to fall down before your mercies for our sins and for the ignorances of the people. Receive our supplication, O God. Make us worthy to offer you supplications, prayers and bloodless sacrifices for all your people. Through the power of your Holy Spirit, enable us, whom you have appointed to this your ministry, to call upon you at every time and in every place, blamelessly and without stumbling, with the pure witness of our conscience, so that you may hear us and be merciful to us in the abundance of your gospel [?].
Deacon:
help us, save us
Exclamation:
For to you belong all glory and honour.
The deacon: Again and again in peace, to the Lord
from above.
of this holy
for our deliverance, and for all who
The priest, a prayer:
Again and many times we fall down before you and entreat you, O Good One who loves humankind, that you look upon our prayer and cleanse our souls and bodies from all defilement of flesh and spirit,
and grant us to stand at your holy altar blamelessly and without condemnation. Grant,
O God, to those who pray with us as well, progress in life, in faith and in spiritual understanding.
Grant them always to serve you with fear and love, to partake of your holy mysteries blamelessly and without condemnation, and to be made worthy of the heavenly kingdom.
The deacon: Help us. Wisdom.
Exclamation:
So that, guarded by your might, to you
and they begin: "We who the Cherubim
The priest says the prayer while bowing: No one who is bound by fleshly desires and pleasures is worthy to come before you, to approach you, or to serve you, O King of glory;
for serving you is great and fearful even to the heavenly powers themselves.

But because of your inexpressible and immeasurable love for mankind, without change and without alteration you appeared to us, and you granted us the priestly celebration of this liturgical and bloodless sacrifice,
as Master of all; for you alone, O Lord our God, reign in the heavens and on earth, seated upon the thrones of the cherubim,
Lord of the seraphim and King of Israel, the only Holy One, who rest among the holy. You, therefore, the only good one who readily hears, I entreat: look upon me,
your sinful and unprofitable servant, and cleanse my soul and heart from an evil conscience, and by the grace of your Holy Spirit make me worthy,
clothed with the grace of the priesthood, to stand before this holy table of yours and to celebrate the sacred rite of your holy and incorruptible body and blood,
for I come to you, bowing my neck, and I entreat you: do not turn your face away from me,
and do not cast me out from among your servants, but deem it fitting that these sacrifices be offered to you by me, your sinful and unworthy servant,
for you are the one who offers and is offered, who receives and is undivided, O Christ our God,
and to you we send up glory, together with your Father, who is without beginning as you are, and your all-holy, good and life-giving Spirit,

And the priest shall begin: "Have mercy on me," and after it the prayer: "O King of heaven, guide of wisdom and bestower of knowledge, teacher of the foolish and helper of the poor, strengthen my heart and make it understanding, O King. Give me a word, O Word of the Father, for behold, I will not keep my lips silent from crying out to you, O King; be merciful to me, who have fallen down before you."

The priest washes his hands. O Lord my God, send down upon me power from on high, and strengthen me for this service of yours, so that I may stand without condemnation before your holy, fearful and awesome altar and offer you the bloodless sacrifice. For yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory, of the Father
The priest shall bow down before the holy table and say: "Magnify the Lord with me, and I will exalt his name together."
They shall answer him: "May the Holy Spirit come upon you, and may the power of the Most High overshadow you."
"Remember us also, master."
The priest shall say: "May the Lord God remember you also in his kingdom always, now and ever and unto the ages."
And he shall bow down before the table once.
The deacon: "Let us complete our prayer to the Lord. For these gifts that have been set forth and sanctified, let us pray to the Lord our God."
"For this holy house."
"For our deliverance and for all who [?]"
The priest's prayer:
"O Lord God,
O Almighty, only Holy One, who accept the sacrifice of praise from those who call upon you with their whole heart,

receive the prayer of us sinners as well, and bring it to your holy altar. Enable us to offer you gifts and spiritual sacrifices for our sins and for the sins of the people committed in ignorance. Make us worthy to find grace before you, so that our sacrifice may be acceptable to you, and so that the good Spirit of your grace may dwell upon us, upon these gifts set before you, and upon all your people.
Deacon: Help us.
That the whole day may be entirely holy, peaceful and without sin, [let us ask] of the Lord.
An angel of peace, a faithful guide, a guardian of our souls and bodies, [let us ask] of the Lord.
Pardon and forgiveness of our sins and transgressions.
Things good and profitable for our souls, and peace for the world, let us ask of the Lord.
That the rest of our life may be spent in peace and worthiness, [let us ask] of the Lord
A Christian end to our life, free of suffering and of shame, and a good defence before the dread judgement seat of Christ, let us ask.
Remembering our all-holy, incorruptible, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, and our holy and God-clad father John Chrysostom,
having remembered [them] together with all the saints, [let us commit] ourselves and one another
and all our life to Christ,
our God,
let us commit.
Exclamation: Through the mercies of your only-begotten Son, with whom you are blessed, together with the all-holy, good and life-giving [?].
Deacon: The doors
People: We believe. Deacon: Let us stand well, let us stand in fear, attend to this holy offering, offered in peace.
People: Mercy, peace.
Priest: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God the Father, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
People: And with your spirit.
Priest: Let us have [our hearts] on high
People: We have them to the Lord.
Priest: ... to the Lord.
People: It is worthy and right.
Priest's prayer: It is worthy and right to praise you, to bless you, to sing hymns to you, to give thanks to you in every place of your dominion.
You are God, beyond words, invisible, beyond understanding. You are forever, as you are, you and your only-begotten Son and your Holy Spirit.

You brought us from nothingness into being, and when we had fallen you raised us up again, and you did not cease doing everything until you had brought us up to heaven and granted us your kingdom to come.
For all these things we thank you, and your only-begotten Son, and your Holy Spirit,
for all things, those we know and those we do not know, for the benefits, seen and unseen, that have been done for us.
We thank you also for this offering, which you have deigned to receive from our hands,
even though thousands of archangels and myriads of angels stand around you, the cherubim and the six-winged, many-eyed seraphim, soaring on their wings.
Exclamation: Singing the hymn of victory, crying out, shouting and saying:
The people: Holy, holy, holy.
The priest's prayer: With these blessed powers we too, O Master, lover of mankind, cry out and say:
You are holy and all-holy, and your glory is great and magnificent,
you who so loved your world that you even gave your only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life;

who came and fulfilled the whole dispensation for our sake, and on the night in which he was betrayed, or rather in which he gave himself up for the life of the world, took bread in his holy and incorruptible
and spotless hands. He gave thanks and blessed it, sanctified it and broke it, and gave it to his holy disciples and apostles, saying:
Exclamation: Take and eat. This is my body, broken for you for the forgiveness of sins.
The priest's prayer: Likewise the cup after supper, saying:
Drink of this, all of you. This is my blood of the new covenant, shed for you, for many, for the forgiveness of sins.
The priest's prayer: Remembering, therefore, this saving commandment and all that was done for us:
the cross, the burial, the three days' [?] sitting [?], and the second and glorious coming again.
Exclamation:
Your own [of your own?] we offer to you, for all things and for all people.
The people: We sing to you, we bless you
The priest's prayer: Again we offer you rational [worship] and entreat you:
Send down your Holy Spirit upon us and upon these gifts that lie before us.
He makes the sign of the cross over the paten and says secretly: And make this bread the precious body of your Christ.
The deacon: Amen.
He makes the sign of the cross over the chalice and says:
And what is in this cup [?] the precious blood of your Christ.
He makes the sign of the cross over both and says: Change them by your Holy Spirit.
Amen.
The priest's prayer: that they may be, for those who receive them, for watchfulness of soul and for the forgiveness of sins,
for communion of your Holy Spirit and for the fulfilment of the kingdom of heaven, not for judgment or condemnation.
Again we offer you this spiritual sacrifice for those who have fallen asleep in faith: the forefathers, the fathers, the patriarchs,
the prophets, the apostles, the preachers, the evangelists, the martyrs, the confessors, the ascetics, and every soul that has died in faith.
Said aloud: Especially for our all-holy, immaculate, most blessed Lady, the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary.
Bowing: For holy John the Prophet,
Forerunner and Baptist; for the holy and all-praised apostles; for saint N. [name to be supplied], whose memory we celebrate; and for all your saints, through whose prayers look upon us, O God.
Remember all who have fallen asleep in the hope of resurrection and eternal life, and give them rest where the light of your face shines on them.
Again we beseech you: remember, Lord, all the people; all orthodox bishops who rightly teach the word of your truth; all the priesthood; the diaconate in Christ; and every order of clergy.
Again we offer you this spiritual worship for the world; for the holy catholic and apostolic Church; for those who live in purity and dignity;
for our faithful and Christ-loving kings, and for all their palace and their soldiers.
Grant them, Lord, a peaceful reign, so that in their tranquillity we too may lead a calm life in all godliness and honour.
Said aloud: First of all, remember, Lord, our archbishop,
whom you have granted to your holy churches: [keep them] in peace, alive, honoured, healthy and long-lived, rightly dividing the word of your truth.
Remember, Lord,
our unworthiness, in the abundance of your mercies.
Forgive me every offence of mine, both voluntary and involuntary, and because of my sins do not withhold the grace of your Holy Spirit from the gifts set before you.
Remember, Lord, the city
in which we live, and all cities and villages, and those who live in them in faith.
Remember, Lord, those at sea, travellers, the sick, those who labour, captives, and their salvation.
Remember, Lord, those who bring offerings and do good works in your holy churches, and those who remember the poor. Send down your mercies on us all.
Said aloud: And grant us, Lord, with one mouth and one heart to glorify and sing praise to your all-honoured and most glorious name, of the Father and the Son [?].
And may the mercies of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ be with all of you. And with your spirit.
The deacon:
Having remembered all the holy fathers, again and again, and always, let us pray to the Lord in peace.
For these precious gifts that have been offered and sanctified, let us beseech the Lord our God,
that God, who loves humankind, having received these upon his holy, heavenly and spiritual altar,
having accepted them as a sweet spiritual fragrance, may send down upon us in return the grace of his Holy Spirit.
To the Lord [?]
That we may be delivered from all [?]
And for all who [?] the help of God
The priest's prayer:
To you we entrust our whole life and our hope, O Master, lover of mankind,
and we call on you, beseech you and take refuge in you: make us worthy to partake with a pure conscience of your holy, heavenly mysteries of this holy and spiritual table,
for the remission of sins and the forgiveness of transgressions, for the communion of the Holy Spirit,
for the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven, not for judgement or condemnation.
The deacon: The whole day [?]
An angel [?]
Good things [?]
Christian [?]
Having asked for the unity of the faith and the communion of the Holy Spirit [?]
Exclamation: And make us worthy, O Master, to dare with boldness and without condemnation to say:
The people: Our Father [?]
The priest: For yours is the kingdom [?]
Peace to all.
The deacon: [?] our heads to the Lord.
The people: O Lord.
Prayer of the priest:
We thank you, invisible King, who by your immeasurable power created all things, and in the abundance of your mercy brought all of us from nothing into being.
Master, look down from heaven on those who have bowed their heads to you, for they have not bowed to flesh and blood but to you, the awesome God. You therefore, Master,
distribute well the things set before all of us, to each according to his need. Sail with those who sail, travel with those who travel, heal the sick, O Physician of souls and bodies.
The exclamation: By the grace, mercy and love for humankind of your only-begotten Son, with whom you are blessed, together with your all-holy
good, and
Look down upon us, O Lord our God, from your holy dwelling place,

from the throne of the glory of your kingdom, and come to sanctify us, you who sit on high with the Father and are also invisibly present here with us. Make us worthy to receive from your mighty hand your incorruptible body and precious blood, and through us all your people.
Deacon: Let us attend.
Priest:
Holy things for the holy.
And when they have completed communion, the deacon:
Let us draw near with faith.
People: Before you, O Lord.
The priest shall give the dismissal: Blessing.
Priest: Be exalted in the heavens, O God.
People: Amen.
Let my mouth be filled.
Deacon:
Stand upright, you who have received the divine, incorruptible, heavenly mysteries; let us give thanks to the Lord.
Help us.
The whole day perfect.
Prayer of the priest:
We thank you, O Lord,
lover of mankind, benefactor of our souls, for on this day too you have made us worthy of your heavenly, immortal mystery.
Direct our ways, save us all in your fear, and guard our life through the prayers and intercession of our Lady,
the Mother of God and ever-virgin Mary, and of all your saints, for you are our sanctifier,
Christ our God, and to you we send up glory, to the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Deacon: Let us go forth in peace to the Lord.
The priest, a prayer:
You who bless those who bless you, O Lord, and sanctify those who hope in you,
save your people and protect the fullness of your Church, and sanctify those who love the beauty of your house;
glorify them in return by your divine power, and do not forsake us, O God, who hope in you;
grant peace to the world, to the churches, to the priests, to our kings, to the soldiers, and to all your people,
for from you comes every good giving, and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from you, from the Father of lights, and to you we send up glory and thanksgiving.
May the name of the Lord be...
The priest: You are the fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets,
Christ our God, who fulfilled the whole plan of the Father; fill our hearts with joy and gladness.
The people: I will bless the Lord.
The priest, a prayer: Having come from strength to strength, we, your sinful and unworthy servants, sing praise to your kingship,
Christ our God;
we have completed the divine service and the mystery. And having come to this second table of yours,
we offer glory, thanksgiving and worship to you, together with the Father who has no beginning and the all-holy, good and life-giving [?], now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.
